papers.relied_on: Abstract-level numbers (UCPCR >=0.28 nmol/nmol, sensitivity 97%, specificity 88%, n=80) as small-cohort accuracy evidence for classifying children as T1D or T2D, and as a UCPCR assay example for row 7.
papers.full_text_shows: The numbers match the abstract (fasting C-peptide 63%/84%, postprandial 87%/86%, UCPCR 97%/88%, ROC AUC 0.974 in the figure legend). The study is a single-centre, prospective case-control comparison of 50 children with T1D and 30 with T2D who were already diagnosed (age over 10 y, duration over 2 y); no islet-antibody or genetic confirmation of the labels is reported, the groups differ in BMI and age at diagnosis (no adjustment), UCPCR was run with a research-type ELISA kit (DRG, Germany) in the hospital laboratory, and the authors state that MODY was not studied. Table 1 is garbled in the extraction (columns mixed), so group medians were not used.
papers.quote: Differentiation between MODY type and T2DM was not performed.
papers.key_numbers: n=80 (50 T1D, 30 T2D); UCPCR cutoff 0.28 nmol/nmol: sensitivity 97%, specificity 88%, AUC 0.974; fasting C-peptide 63%/84%; postprandial C-peptide 87%/86%; UCPCR sample 2 h after lunch, boric acid, same-day or refrigerated overnight; intra-assay CV <3.1%
papers.role_in_work: Diagnostic accuracy evidence for UCPCR in youth (row 33); UCPCR protocol and assay example (row 7 D4). Not a MODY source.
papers.design: Prospective single-centre case-control diagnostic study with data-derived ROC cutoff, no external validation
papers.population_and_size: 80 children and adolescents over 10 years with diabetes for over 2 years, normal renal function, Tanta University Hospital, Egypt
papers.measure_type: C-peptide: post-meal urinary C-peptide:creatinine ratio (2 h after lunch), plus fasting and postprandial serum C-peptide (postprandial timing not stated in the text read)
papers.assay_or_platform: Human C-peptide ELISA kit (DRG Instruments GmbH, Germany) for serum and urine; chemistry analyser INDIKO PLUS for creatinine; no US-marketed assay named
papers.quality_note: Small, single-centre, known-diagnosis design (spectrum bias likely); labels not antibody- or gene-verified; cutoff derived and tested in the same sample; no conflict of interest declared. Text extraction is partial (table garbled).

papers.relied_on: ISPAD 2022 lists detectable C-peptide as one feature that should make clinicians doubt a type 1 label, but gives no recommendation to measure it.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed. C-peptide appears once as a suspicion feature ('detectable C-peptide, either in blood or urine, over an extended partial remission phase, at least 5 years after diagnosis'), listed with antibody absence and family history, and the text says none of these features is pathognomonic and they should be considered together. Other C-peptide mentions describe low or undetectable levels in KATP neonatal diabetes. The recommendation boxes for MODY testing name family history, GCK hyperglycaemia and absence of T1D/T2D characteristics, not a C-peptide measurement. No assay, threshold, measure type or timing is given.
papers.quote: detectable C‐peptide (either in blood or urine) over an extended partial remission phase (at least 5 years after diagnosis)
papers.key_numbers: Monogenic diabetes about 2.5%-6.5% of paediatric diabetes; 3% of obese youth with presumed T2D carried pathogenic variants (cited study); C-peptide persistence criterion: at least 5 years after diagnosis (not 2 years)
papers.role_in_work: Paediatric guideline text for D3 on rows 7 and 33
papers.population_and_size: Children and adolescents with suspected monogenic diabetes; no study size
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, blood or urine, no timing specified (partial-remission feature, not a test recommendation)
papers.quality_note: Good text (PMC XML). Conflict of interest: one author advised on a glibenclamide suspension; others none. Executive summary lists were partly stripped in earlier reads but the feature list is complete here.

papers.relied_on: PMDI 2023 as a systematic review with expert recommendations that sets out who to test, with C-peptide as one triage component, and the biomarker-pathway PPV of 20%.
papers.full_text_shows: The graded review (100 studies, GRADE for test strategies) states that the best evidence (level 1) supports testing people under 30 years who are non-obese and either autoantibody negative and/or have retained C-peptide. C-peptide is an alternative to antibodies, not a required step, and no threshold, timing or assay is defined. The text gives PPV 20% for the antibody/C-peptide biomarker pathway versus PPV 40% and 55% of cases missed for a calculator probability above 25%, and PPV 58% with 63% missed for traditional MODY criteria. Limitations: most studies were cohort or cross-sectional with biased selection, only subsets were genetically tested, false negatives could not be counted, and recommendations rest mostly on yields in different populations.
papers.quote: who are either autoantibody negative and/or have retained C-peptide levels
papers.key_numbers: 100 studies for who-to-test; 60 studies for the age/antibody/C-peptide/non-obese criterion; large-panel yield 0.7%-34%; suspected-MODY cohorts 16%-23%; 18/2670 (0.7%) yield in antibody-negative adults diagnosed over 40 y; biomarker pathway PPV 20%
papers.role_in_work: Consensus-level source for D3, D2 and D1 on row 7 (who gets a gene panel)
papers.design: Systematic review with GRADE and expert consensus recommendations (PMDI, international)
papers.population_and_size: People with diabetes, all ages; 12,896 records screened, 100 studies included for who to test
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, not further specified (retained C-peptide as a way to lower the probability of T1D); post-meal urinary ratio is not discussed in the text lines read
papers.assay_or_platform: None specified for C-peptide; genetic reference standard is a large gene panel
papers.quality_note: Good text. Competing-interest statement not found in the extracted text. Diagnostic-yield evidence with selection bias, as the authors state.

papers.relied_on: ANZ 2025 consensus as non-US consensus text that endorses C-peptide as a triage component for gene testing and, for row 35, contains no insulin, C-peptide or HOMA-IR recommendation in pregnancy.
papers.full_text_shows: A graded [Strong] recommendation says large-panel testing is recommended in non-obese people diagnosed before 30 years with negative pancreatic autoantibodies and/or a retained serum C-peptide response to hyperglycaemia; it adopts the PMDI Grade A/B groups. C-peptide is therefore an alternative to antibodies, with no threshold or timing given. The Exeter calculator is endorsed at 25% (10% if early insulin). For GDM the text only says GCK testing should be considered in non-obese women with fasting glucose above 5.5 mmol/L; a keyword search of the text found no HOMA-IR, fasting insulin or C-peptide use in pregnancy. Testing is requested by endocrinologists or genetics services; no conflict statement was found in the extracted text. It says nothing about first-trimester HOMA-IR, so it cannot support or refute row 35 part (b).
papers.quote: negative pancreatic autoantibodies and/or a retained serum C‐peptide response to hyperglycaemia
papers.key_numbers: Recommendation graded [Strong]; age under 30 y; non-obese; calculator threshold 25% (10% if early insulin); GCK in GDM: fasting glucose above 5.5 mmol/L, 'should be considered'; more than 80% of monogenic diabetes undiagnosed or misdiagnosed (cited)
papers.role_in_work: Consensus source for D3, D2, D1, D5 on row 7; negative source (absence of text) for D3 on row 35
papers.design: Joint society consensus statement, 11 experts, graded strong or weak
papers.population_and_size: Adults with suspected monogenic diabetes (Australia and New Zealand); no study size
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, serum, 'response to hyperglycaemia' (stimulated or post-meal wording, not defined); no insulin or HOMA-IR measure in the pregnancy section
papers.assay_or_platform: None named for C-peptide; NGS panel for genetics
papers.quality_note: Good text. Non-US body (clarification 6) but it adopts the international PMDI recommendation. No threshold or protocol for the C-peptide criterion.

papers.relied_on: An externally validated biomarker-inclusive calculator: adding C-peptide and antibodies raised AUC from 0.80 to 0.98 in early-insulin-treated people; biomarkers alone gave 0.96.
papers.full_text_shows: Numbers confirmed. The biomarker variable is binary and combines C-peptide with antibodies (type 1-consistent if C-peptide negative or any antibody positive; antibodies were only measured when C-peptide was retained), so the C-peptide contribution cannot be separated. External validation had only 5 monogenic cases among 940 early-insulin-treated people (0.5%) and 15 of 85 in the other model; the population is White European only; biomarker data were absent from the training and primary-care datasets. The text also reports that testing everyone who is C-peptide positive and antibody negative covers 17.2% with PPV 14.8% and no cases missed, versus 2.8% eligible, PPV 40.5% and 54.5% of cases missed with traditional criteria.
papers.quote: MD cases (n=5; 0.5%) had a much higher predicted mean probability
papers.key_numbers: Early-insulin model AUC 0.98 (CrI 0.95-0.98) vs 0.80 clinical-only vs 0.96 biomarkers alone (p=0.046); external AUC 0.98 on 5 cases, not-early model 0.92 on 15 cases; 5% threshold gives positive test rate 16%-19%; C-peptide cut-offs UCPCR 0.2 nmol/mmol, unfasted plasma 200 pmol/L, fasted plasma 80 pmol/L
papers.role_in_work: D8 evidence for C-peptide plus antibodies over clinical features (row 7); supporting accuracy evidence for D2
papers.design: Prediction-model development with internal bootstrap validation and small external validation; calibration in UK primary-care records
papers.population_and_size: UNITED (UK, development; 455 early-insulin-treated, 177 monogenic) plus MY DIABETES and UNITED paediatric external sets; CPRD 67,827 for calibration
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (urinary ratio, unfasted or fasted plasma) combined with islet antibodies; mixed random and fasting sampling
papers.assay_or_platform: UCPCR and plasma C-peptide in UK research cohorts (assay limit 27 pmol/L in MY DIABETES); platform not named in the text read; GAD and IA2 antibodies; Exeter NGS panels
papers.quality_note: Good text (author manuscript). External validation is very small for monogenic cases; White European only; abstract AUC 0.98 comes from the development cohort. All authors declare no competing interests.

papers.relied_on: ProDiGY: 2.8% monogenic diabetes among youth with presumed T2D, used as a check that the number who have MODY is far below the number in whom the question arises.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed: 93 of 3,333 youth (2.8%) carried a pathogenic or likely pathogenic MODY variant (HNF1A 1.3%, GCK 0.7%, HNF4A 0.5%). The cohort was selected: TODAY required negative antibodies and fasting C-peptide above 0.6 ng/mL, so it excluded the youth most likely to have MODY. Fasting C-peptide (AUC 0.67), age at diagnosis (0.59) and HDL (0.66) could not identify MODY, and combined AUC was 0.76; the authors note UCPCR is not often performed in the US.
papers.quote: neither facilitated clear discrimination of MODY from non-MODY diabetes, alone or in combination
papers.key_numbers: 93/3,333 = 2.8%; fasting C-peptide AUC 0.67; combined AUC 0.76; 83 of 93 (89%) had a result that would change management, but most were not on indicated treatment (GCK: 34.8% appropriately untreated)
papers.role_in_work: Prevalence cross-check for D7 on row 7; shows fasting C-peptide has no triage value in antibody-negative youth with presumed T2D
papers.design: Cross-sectional whole-exome sequencing analysis of three US cohorts
papers.population_and_size: 3,333 youth with clinician-diagnosed type 2 diabetes before age 20 (SEARCH 492, TODAY 511, TODAY Genetics 2,330)
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, fasting (blood); no post-meal or stimulated measure
papers.assay_or_platform: Not named in the text read; fasting C-peptide measured at baseline in TODAY and SEARCH
papers.quality_note: Good text; large, multiethnic, US. Selection by antibody status and C-peptide limits generalisation. No D7 count can be taken from it.

papers.relied_on: SEARCH counts of 18,169 type 1 and 5,293 type 2 cases as annual new youth cases (row 7 chain), and 2017-2018 age counts (179, 341, 445, 194) with incidence 22.2 per 100,000 (rows 29 and 33).
papers.full_text_shows: The 18,169 and 5,293 figures are SEARCH registry totals for 2002-2018 (17 years; 85 and 44 million person-years), not annual 2017-2018 counts and not national counts. The text gives adjusted incidence for 2017-2018 of 22.2 per 100,000 for T1D (rise 2.02% per year) and 17.9 per 100,000 for T2D (rise 5.31% per year); peak age 10 y for T1D and 16 y for T2D. The age counts 179, 341, 445 and 194 are not in the stored text (the XML has no tables), so they could not be checked.
papers.quote: From 2002 through 2018, SEARCH identified 18,169 youth with T1D among 85 million person-years of youth aged 0–19 years
papers.key_numbers: T1D 18,169 cases and T2D 5,293 over 17 years; 2017-2018 incidence T1D 22.2 and T2D 17.9 per 100,000 per year; completeness 97-99% (T1D), 91-96% (T2D)
papers.role_in_work: Epidemiology source for D7 chains on rows 7, 29 and 33
papers.population_and_size: US youth in five SEARCH surveillance areas, 2002-2018; 18,169 T1D and 5,293 T2D registered cases
papers.measure_type: Not applicable (incidence of diabetes; no insulin or C-peptide measure)
papers.quality_note: Text partial: tables missing from the stored XML. High-quality registry (capture-recapture completeness reported). The rate is for the surveillance areas; a national count needs a US population denominator that the paper does not give.

papers.relied_on: Igls consensus: C-peptide (basal and stimulated) is one of four criteria that classify graft function; pre-transplant testing is critical; no numeric threshold for clinically significant C-peptide was recorded.
papers.full_text_shows: Optimal, good and marginal tiers all require documentation of an increase in C-peptide over the pretransplant value, so every non-failed tier depends on the measure, and the conclusion says success should require restoration of clinically significant C-peptide. A numeric minimum is given in the functional goal and the conclusion (above 0.5 ng/ml or 0.17 nmol/l); it is not the tier definition. The text says C-peptide should be measured before transplant, fasting with a concomitant glucose, with or without stimulated measures, the same way before and after; stimulation with arginine or glucagon is called gold standard but not widely available; very low levels of questionable significance (below 0.3 ng/ml fasting or 0.6 ng/ml postprandial) are often detected despite graft failure; interpretation depends on glucose, insulin sensitivity and renal clearance. The authors call the classification a work in progress that should be validated.
papers.quote: restoration of clinically significant C-peptide production (>0.5 ng/ml or >0.17 nmol/l)
papers.key_numbers: Success: HbA1c below 7.0%, no severe hypoglycaemia, over 50% insulin reduction, C-peptide above 0.5 ng/ml (0.17 nmol/l); optimal also needs HbA1c 6.5% or below and no insulin; four tiers
papers.role_in_work: Consensus source for D3, D1, D5, D6 and S on row 10 (graft function)
papers.design: Consensus report from an international workshop (IPITA/EPITA opinion leaders)
papers.population_and_size: Recipients of islet or pancreas transplants (and candidates for beta-cell replacement); no study size
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, fasting with concomitant glucose, with or without stimulated (mixed-meal, arginine or glucagon)
papers.quality_note: Good text. Opinion-leader consensus, not a formal guideline; authors state it should be validated; no conflict statement found in the extracted text.

proposals.reason: The youth counts used in the chain (18,169 and 5,293 called annual) are 2002-2018 SEARCH registry totals. Rebuilt from the paper's 2017-2018 rates (22.2 and 17.9 per 100,000 per year) and an assumed US youth population of about 83 million aged 0-19 and 43 million aged 10-19 [recall], the youth part is about 18,000 T1D and 7,700 T2D a year, so the chain total changes by about 10% and the bin stays 3 (low confidence, bin 2 or 3). Fix the label, not the score.
proposals.quote: From 2002 through 2018, SEARCH identified 18,169 youth with T1D among 85 million person-years of youth aged 0–19 years

proposals.reason: C058 used a research-type ELISA kit in a hospital laboratory with a timed post-meal sample; nothing in it addresses US-marketed assays. Under clarification 25 (adopted, not yet applied) the limiting assay would be post-meal UCPCR, which the C256 authors say is not often performed in the US, so a later rescoring could consider 1 with blood C-peptide [3] in brackets; the evidence for that is not in C058 alone, so no change is proposed here.
proposals.quote: Urine containers with boric acid preservative were used.

proposals.reason: Units V4 and V5. C100 and C121 make retained C-peptide an alternative to negative antibodies inside a graded recommendation, which could be read as 3 under clarification 15 (other tests can substitute). Not proposed: the pathway PPV is 20%, the criteria also need age and non-obesity, guideline status is already carried by D3 (3), and the final decision is made by the gene test.
proposals.quote: who are either autoantibody negative and/or have retained C-peptide levels

proposals.reason: Unit V4. In the Igls text every tier other than failed requires documented C-peptide rise over the pretransplant value, and success 'should require' clinically significant C-peptide; no other test can stand in for that component. Under clarification 15 this reads as a required result for the classification decision. Counter-argument: the criteria name no treatment action and Igls is an opinion-leader consensus, so 3 stays defensible (and clarification 29 would cap a pure research-outcome reading). Main session to decide.
proposals.quote: documentation of an increase over pretransplant measurement of C-peptide

proposals.reason: Unit V5; same evidence and same counter-argument as unit V4. V5 gave 3 because other criteria cover part of the decision, but the tier definitions make the C-peptide component mandatory for any non-failed grade.
proposals.quote: documentation of an increase over pretransplant measurement of C-peptide

proposals.reason: Unit V1. The text says C-peptide should be measured before transplantation to determine posttransplant graft function and is critical to inform monitoring: a recommended step (3). 'Should', an opinion-leader workshop and the authors' note that the criteria need validation do not reach a requirement for the decision (clarification 13), so 4 is not supported.
proposals.quote: Thus, levels of C-peptide should be measured prior to transplantation in order to determine posttransplant graft function.

proposals.reason: Unit V1 (corrected score 3). C100 and C121 contain the C-peptide criterion in a graded recommendation (ANZ [Strong], adopting PMDI Grade A/B groups), which supports 3 for the population non-obese and diagnosed under 30. ISPAD (C091) alone would give 2: it lists detectable C-peptide as a suspicion feature and recommends no measurement.
proposals.quote: negative pancreatic autoantibodies and/or a retained serum C‐peptide response to hyperglycaemia

proposals.reason: Unit V8. ISPAD 2022 is the paediatric body and gives no recommendation to measure C-peptide, only a suspicion feature at least 5 years after diagnosis, so 2 stands; it does not cover the over-2-year window of the row.
proposals.quote: detectable C‐peptide (either in blood or urine) over an extended partial remission phase (at least 5 years after diagnosis)

proposals.reason: Unit V9. C058 confirms the numbers but adds that labels were not antibody- or gene-verified, groups differed in BMI and age at diagnosis, and the cutoff is data-derived; observational accuracy (2) fits and nothing supports 3.
proposals.quote: UCPCR had a sensitivity of 97%, a specificity of 88% at a cutoff point

proposals.reason: Unit V9. C058 compares only C-peptide variants with each other (UCPCR 97%/88%, postprandial 87%/86%, fasting 63%/84%); it has no comparison with antibodies, genetics or BMI, so mechanism-only 2 stands (clarification 19).
proposals.quote: Fasting C-peptide had a sensitivity of 63%, a specificity of 84%

proposals.reason: Unit V8 (corrected score 2). The paper confirms 22.2 per 100,000 in 2017-2018 and an annual rise of about 2%, as used in the chain; the age counts 179, 341, 445 and 194 could not be checked in the stored text (no tables). No change.

claim_issues.issue: The PMDI full text reports it: PPV 20% for the antibody/C-peptide biomarker pathway, compared with PPV 40% (55% of cases missed) for a calculator probability above 25% and PPV 58% (63% missed) for traditional criteria. The primary study behind the figures was not traced in this text.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: PMDI 2023 (full text) reports a PPV of 20% for the antibody-negative/retained-C-peptide pathway, versus 40% (55% of cases missed) for a calculator probability above 25% and 58% (63% missed) for traditional MODY criteria; the primary source of these figures is not named in the sentence.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 7, sources: 'UCPCR studies PMIDs 21270186, 23289766, 25792383, 32052124' and 'ISPAD C-peptide wording unread'
claim_issues.issue: PMID 32052124 (Elzahar 2020) compares T1D with T2D in already-diagnosed children and states that MODY was not studied, so it is not a MODY-triage source. The ISPAD wording is now read in full text.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: PMID 32052124 (DOI 10.1007/s00431-020-03606-7, full text) tested UCPCR for T1D versus T2D in children; MODY was not studied. ISPAD 2022 (full text) lists detectable C-peptide, blood or urine, at least 5 years after diagnosis as one suspicion feature for monogenic diabetes and recommends no measurement.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 10, caveats: 'it gives no numeric threshold for clinically significant C-peptide'
claim_issues.issue: The Igls text states one in its functional goal and its conclusion (above 0.5 ng/ml or 0.17 nmol/l); the tier definitions themselves use an increase over the pretransplant value.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Igls 2018 (full text) states a minimum of above 0.5 ng/ml (0.17 nmol/l) as clinically significant C-peptide in its functional goal and conclusion, while the tier definitions require a rise over the pretransplant value; it also says levels below 0.3 ng/ml fasting or 0.6 ng/ml postprandial are often detected despite graft failure, and that the criteria are a work in progress to be validated.

claim_issues.issue: In Elzahar 2020 the 2-h post-lunch sample was collected for the study and sent to the laboratory the same day or refrigerated overnight; home collection is only suggested in the discussion. The labels were not antibody- or gene-verified. ISPAD describes preserved C-peptide at least 5 years after diagnosis, not over 2 years.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: UCPCR (post-meal, 2 h after lunch, boric acid) separated T1D from T2D in 80 Egyptian children with diabetes over 2 years (cutoff 0.28 nmol/nmol, sensitivity 97%, specificity 88%); diagnoses were not antibody- or gene-verified and MODY was not studied. ISPAD 2022 uses at least 5 years of detectable C-peptide as its doubt-the-T1D feature.

The paper has no text on HOMA-IR, fasting insulin or C-peptide in pregnancy; it supports only the negative (no insulin recommendation in pregnancy) and the glucose-based GCK trigger (part a). notes: Texts read from corpus/fulltext (C058 and C186 are PDF extractions; C091, C100, C121, C256, C274 and C050 are PMC XML). C058 Table 1 is garbled and was not used. C274 XML has no tables, so Table 1 and appendix numbers were not checked. Competing-interest statements were not found in the extracted text of C100, C121 and C050 (not found in the extracted text, not necessarily absent). Current scores: row 7 V1 D3 = 3 (corrected from 2 after the stage 3 skeptic pass), row 7 V5 S = 1 (corrected), row 29 V8 D7 = 2 (corrected from 3); all other cited entries read at their original score; V7 supersedes U1 only for D7. US population denominators (about 83 million youth 0-19, 43 million aged 10-19) are [recall], not from the paper. Path to viability: row 7 unaffected (a C-peptide threshold and timing for the retained-C-peptide criterion remain undefined in C100, C121 and C091; C186 shows UCPCR 0.2 nmol/mmol and plasma cut-offs in UK cohorts only); row 33 path should add that C058 has no antibody or gene verification and no MODY arm, so a study with a genetic reference standard is the missing piece; row 10 unaffected, though the Igls authors state the criteria still need validation. Proposed changes are two low-confidence D1 raises on row 10 for the main session to accept or reject; no other score is proposed to change. Tool calls used: 30 including the two writes and the final report. Assumption: the 'biomarker pathway' figures in C186 (17.2% eligible, PPV 14.8%, 54.5% missed) refer to the UNITED early-insulin-treated data; the passage did not name the dataset in the lines read.
